issue.title: Evaluate Hydrogen default promotion and Carbon or Orchestrator catalog eligibility
issue.description: Proposing bead: sase-1ss.1, PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #5. The completed epic keeps agy tiers on 3.8 Flash and leaves every size-alias pool unchanged. Its accepted research reports Hydrogen in the official all-plans table but requires a confirmed Free-account probe before promotion. This landing verified agy 1.5.8 lists all four Hydrogen slugs and gemini-pro-orchestrator-g1-pro on the current host; that does not establish this account is Free. No Carbon slug appears. First obtain auditable Free-plan availability evidence without changing defaults on assumption. Then decide whether Hydrogen belongs in large/small tiers or the size-alias ladder, respecting decisions:size-alias-effort-ladder, descending efforts, provider redundancy, and fixed-effort slugs until explicit-effort support exists. Separately evaluate Carbon slug/entitlements and Orchestrator planner/executor handoffs under SASE no-progress supervision before choosing to catalog them. Record deliberate decline/defer outcomes if eligibility is unproven; do not manufacture slugs or enable an opaque model simply because the live list includes it. Large because the rollout/policy and orchestrator behavior require investigation, not a mechanical YAML replacement.

task_type_fields.proposal: Gather Free-plan and capability evidence, then decide Hydrogen tier/ladder promotion and Carbon/Orchestrator membership.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: The approved sase-1ss scope explicitly postpones these policy changes and leaves current tiers, aliases, and excluded model families fixed.

issue.creation_reason: Proposed by sase-1ss.1 note #5; the accepted design deliberately retains stable Flash tiers and postpones new default and model-membership decisions pending account and capability evidence.

payload.description: Optional-model eligibility and default promotion are distinct from reconciling already-supported catalog families.
